title: The frame budget
description:
`SetTargetFPS(60)` gives each frame a **budget** of 1000 / 60 = 16.7 milliseconds for input, update and drawing. Write three small helpers a game's debug overlay uses:

```cpp
double frameBudgetMs(int fps);                 // 1000 / fps; 0 when fps <= 0 (no limit)
int framesFor(double seconds, int fps);        // how many frames that many seconds takes, rounded to the nearest
std::string fpsLabel(double frameTimeSeconds); // "60 FPS (16.7 ms)"
```

`fpsLabel` shows the frames per second as `1 / frameTime` rounded to the nearest whole number, and the frame time in milliseconds with one decimal place. A frame time of 0 or less gives `"-- FPS"`.
hints: `std::lround` rounds to the nearest whole number; `snprintf` with `%.1f` gives one decimal place.
lessonTitle: What raylib Is and Setting It Up
